title: 第十五章 夜航船第十六章 钦差驾到
content_zh:
子时，珠江上起了雾。
不是那种铺天盖地的浓雾，而是贴着水面的一层薄纱，刚好没过船舷，把船底隐在雾气里，远远看去就像几条船悬在云端。
何成局蹲在其中一条小船的船头，手按着腰间的笑面虎短刀，眼睛一眨不眨地盯着码头方向。
三条小船藏在芦苇荡里，船身用黑布蒙了，连船桨都包了棉布，划水时几乎不出声。范老六的五个徒弟各就各位，每人手里一根长篙，篙头也裹了布。范老六本人蹲在何成局旁边，嘴里嚼着一根草茎，时不时吐出一口唾沫。
“二爷，子时过了。”范老六把草茎吐掉，“潘老爷的人该到了。”
话音刚落，码头方向传来三声布谷鸟叫。
何成局把手指含在嘴里，回了三声。
片刻之后，十几个黑影从码头的暗处鱼贯而出。为首的是潘启明的心腹管家吴管家，身后跟着十几个力夫，每人肩上扛着一捆布匹。布匹看上去就是普通的棉布，粗麻绳捆着，外面裹一层油布防潮。但何成局知道，布捆里面掏空了，塞的是印度鸦片。
吴管家走到岸边，压低了声音：“何二爷，货都在这儿了。总共四十捆，每捆里面藏了五盒烟土，正好两百盒。”
“官兵换岗了？”何成局问。
“刚换。下一班还有一个时辰。”吴管家擦了擦额头的汗，声音有些发紧，“码头上那两队官兵今晚加了一班巡逻，比平时多了一倍人手。货是从仓库后门搬出来的，绕了三条巷子才到这儿。”
何成局点点头，朝范老六打了个手势。
范老六把草茎往嘴里一塞，无声地挥了挥手。五条黑影从芦苇荡里钻出来，是那五个徒弟。他们和十几个力夫一起，像蚂蚁搬家一样把布捆一捆一捆往船上递。没人说话，没人咳嗽，连脚步都踩在泥地最软的地方，几乎不出声。
何成局也加入了搬运。他扛起一捆布匹，掂了掂分量——一捆约莫三十斤，四十捆就是一千二百，斤。三条小船分摊，每条载重四百斤，再加上六个人，勉强在吃水线以内。
搬运只用了不到一炷香。
吴管家临走前拉了一下何成局的袖子：“何二爷，老爷说了，这批货运到佛山之后，霍老板那边会付你第一笔酬劳，三百两。剩下的等货出手之后再结。”
“行。”何成局没有多说。
“还有一件事。”吴管家的声音压得更低了，“老爷让我提醒你，最近斧头帮的人在打听你的行踪。今晚的事，他们可能听到了风声。”
何成局眉头一皱：“他们知道了？”
“不一定知道具体时间和路线，但知道你今晚有大动作。”吴管家说完，匆匆拱手，带着力夫们消失在黑暗里。

何成局站在岸边，看着那十几个黑影融入夜色，然后转身跳上船头。
“开船。”他说。
范老六把草茎一吐，长篙在水里轻轻一点，小船无声无息地滑出了芦苇荡。
三条小船排成一线，保持着约莫十丈的间距，沿着江岸的阴影缓缓行驶。岸上的官兵灯笼在雾里变成一团团模糊的黄光，看起来很近，实际上隔着老远。
何成局蹲在船头，一只手搭在船舷上，一只手握着刀柄。江风吹在脸上，带着水腥味和雾气的湿润。
他在想吴管家最后那句话。
斧头帮在打听他的行踪。
雷虎这个人，蝎子说得对——睚眦必报，但不莽撞。他不会直接带人冲上门来砍，而是会找个最阴损的时机捅刀子。今晚的运货路线，雷虎不一定知道，但如果他派人盯住了春香楼，就会发现何成局今晚不在。
一个二当家深夜外出，带了六个撑船手，走的是水路。聪明人不难猜出他在干什么。
“范老哥，”何成局忽然开口，“这条水路上，有斧头帮的人吗？”
范老六沉默了一下，手里的长篙在水里划了个圈：“二爷，广州城外的水道上，哪个帮派都有人。斧头帮在珠江上有两条船，平时用来运私盐。他们的水上头目叫陈三水，人送外号‘混江泥鳅’，水性极好。不过他们的活动范围在狮子洋一带，离咱们要走的水道还远。”
“如果他们要截咱们，最可能在哪里动手？”
范老六想了想，伸手指向前方远处：“过了前面那片乱葬岗，河道会收窄，两岸是密林，只有一条水道能走。如果要在水上设伏，那里是最合适的地方。”
何成局顺着他的手指看过去。雾气里隐约能看到远处有一片黑黢黢的阴影，那就是乱葬岗——一片连绵的荒坟，长满了野草和矮树，歪歪斜斜的墓碑像一根根折断的骨头戳在土里。
“那片乱葬岗，”何成局问，“水里能藏人吗？”
“能。”范老六的语气变得很古怪，“但不光能藏活人。二爷，您信不信鬼神？”
何成局笑了一声：“不信。”
“那您胆子比我大。”范老六把长篙往水里一插，小船微微拐了个弯，“我在这条水道上走了四十年，那片乱葬岗下面，可不光是坟。早年间打仗的时候，死尸都是直接往江里扔的。后来闹瘟疫，整村整村的人死了没人收尸，也是往江里倒。水底下那些白骨，堆得比船舷还高。有时候晚上撑船经过，篙子会碰到水底的东西，拔都拔不出来。”
他话音刚落，船底就传来“咚”的一声闷响。
几个徒弟同时停住了篙。黑暗中看不清他们的表情，但能看到他们的身体都绷紧了。

范老六面不改色地把长篙往水里戳了戳，然后拔出来：“树根。大惊小怪。”他回头瞪了徒弟们一眼，但何成局注意到他握着长篙的手紧了紧。
小船继续往前。
雾气越来越浓，岸上的灯火已经彻底看不见了，只有月亮透过雾层洒下一层惨淡的白光。两岸的荒坟在雾里若隐若现，有些坟头已经塌了，露出半边棺材板。偶尔有夜鸟从坟头上扑棱棱飞起，叫声像是婴儿在哭。
何成局倒是没什么感觉。他不信鬼神，只信手里的刀。但他能感觉到船上的气氛在变——那几个徒弟的呼吸明显急促了，划篙的动作也变得僵硬。
“别慌。”何成局的声音不大，但在安静的江面上传得很远，“死人不会咬人，活人才会。把精神放在活人身上。”
content_en:
At midnight, there was fog on the Pearl River.
It's not the kind of thick fog that covers the sky, but a layer of gauze clinging to the water, just covering the side of the ship, hiding the bottom of the ship in the fog. From a distance, it looks like several ships hanging in the clouds.
He Chengju squatted on the bow of one of the boats, holding the smiling tiger dagger at his waist and staring unblinkingly in the direction of the dock.
Three small boats were hidden in the reeds. The hulls were covered with black cloth, and even the oars were wrapped in cotton cloth. They made almost no sound when paddling. Fan Laoliu's five apprentices took their places, each holding a long pole with its ends wrapped in cloth. Fan Laoliu himself squatted next to He Chengju, chewing a grass stalk and spitting from time to time.
"Second Master, it's past time." Fan Laoliu spat out the grass stalks, "It's time for Master Pan's people to arrive."
As soon as he finished speaking, three cuckoo calls came from the direction of the pier.
He Chengju put his fingers in his mouth and replied three times.
A moment later, a dozen black figures filed out of the darkness of the dock. The leader was Pan Qiming's confidant butler Wu Butler, followed by a dozen Lifu, each carrying a bundle of cloth on their shoulders. The cloth looked like ordinary cotton, tied with coarse hemp rope, and wrapped with a layer of oilcloth to prevent moisture. But He Chengju knew that the cloth bundle was hollowed out and stuffed with Indian opium.
Butler Wu walked to the shore and lowered his voice: "Master He, the goods are all here. There are forty bundles in total, and there are five boxes of cigarettes hidden in each bundle, which is exactly two hundred boxes."
"Is there a change of guard among the officers and soldiers?" He Chengju asked.
"Just changed. The next shift is still an hour away." Steward Wu wiped the sweat from his forehead, his voice a little tight, "The two teams of officers and soldiers on the pier are doing an extra patrol tonight, with twice the manpower than usual. The goods were moved out of the back door of the warehouse and took three detours to get here."
He Chengju nodded and gestured to Fan Laoliu.
Fan Laoliu stuffed the grass stalk into his mouth and waved his hand silently. Five black shadows emerged from the reeds, they were the five disciples. Together with more than a dozen laborers, they delivered bundles of cloth to the ship like ants moving. No one spoke, no one coughed, even the footsteps stepped on the softest part of the mud, making almost no sound.
He Chengju also joined in the transportation. He picked up a bundle of cloth and weighed it - one bundle weighed about thirty kilograms, and forty bundles equaled one thousand, two hundred kilograms. Divided among three boats, each carrying four hundred kilograms, plus six people, they were barely within the waterline.
It only took less than one stick of incense to carry it.
Butler Wu pulled He Chengju's sleeve before leaving: "Master He, I said that after this shipment arrives in Foshan, Boss Huo will pay you the first payment, three hundred taels. The rest will be paid after the goods are sold."
"Okay." He Chengju didn't say much.
"There's one more thing." Butler Wu's voice dropped even lower, "Master asked me to remind you that people from the Ax Gang have been inquiring about your whereabouts recently. They may have heard about what happened tonight."
He Chengju frowned: "Do they know?"
"I don't necessarily know the specific time and route, but I know that you have a big move tonight." After Butler Wu finished speaking, he hurriedly handed over his hands and disappeared into the darkness with the Lifus.
He Chengju stood on the shore, watching the dozen black figures blending into the night, then turned around and jumped onto the bow of the boat.
"Sail the boat," he said.
Fan Laoliu spit out the grass stems, dipped his long pole in the water, and the boat slipped out of the reed swamp silently.
Three small boats lined up in a line, keeping a distance of about ten feet, and drove slowly along the shadow of the river bank. The lanterns of the officers and soldiers on the shore turned into blurry yellow lights in the fog. They looked very close, but in fact they were far away.
He Chengju squatted on the bow of the boat, with one hand on the side of the boat and the other holding the handle of the knife. The river breeze blew on my face, bringing with it the smell of water and the moisture of mist.
He was thinking about Butler Wu's last words.
The Ax Gang is inquiring about his whereabouts.
As for Lei Hu, Scorpion is right - he will retaliate, but he will not be reckless. He won't just bring people to the door.Instead of cutting, he will find the most sinister opportunity to stab him. Lei Hu may not necessarily know tonight's cargo route, but if he sends people to keep an eye on Chunxiang Tower, he will find that He Chengju is not here tonight.
A second-in-command went out late at night, taking six punters with him, and took the waterway. It is not difficult for a smart person to guess what he is doing.
"Brother Fan," He Chengju suddenly said, "Are there anyone from the Ax Gang on this waterway?"
Fan Laoliu was silent for a moment, and drew a circle in the water with the long pole in his hand: "Second Master, there are people from every gang on the waterways outside Guangzhou. The Ax Gang has two boats on the Pearl River, which are usually used to transport smuggled salt. Their leader on the water is called Chen Sanshui, who is nicknamed 'Hunjiang Loach' because of his excellent water properties. However, their activity range is in the Lion Ocean area, which is far away from the waterway we are going to take."
"If they wanted to intercept us, where would they most likely do it?"
Fan Laoliu thought for a while and pointed far ahead: "After passing the mass graves in front, the river will narrow. There are dense forests on both sides, and there is only one waterway to walk on. If you want to set up an ambush on the water, that is the most suitable place."
He Chengju followed his finger and looked over. In the mist, you can vaguely see a dark shadow in the distance, which is the mass grave - a continuous barren grave, covered with weeds and short trees, with crooked tombstones poking into the soil like broken bones.
"That mass grave," He Chengju asked, "can anyone hide in the water?"
"Yes." Fan Laoliu's tone became very strange, "But it can not only hide living people. Second Master, do you believe in ghosts and gods?"
He Chengju laughed: "I don't believe it."
"Then you are braver than me." Fan Laoliu plunged the long pole into the water, and the boat turned slightly. "I have been walking on this waterway for forty years. There are more than just graves under the mass graves. During the war in the early years, the dead bodies were thrown directly into the water. They were thrown into the river. Later, when there was a plague, people in the whole village were dead and no one was collecting their bodies, so they were dumping them into the river. Sometimes when a boat was passing by at night, the poles would hit things on the bottom of the water and they could not be pulled out. "
As soon as he finished speaking, there was a muffled sound from the bottom of the boat.
Several apprentices stopped their poles at the same time. I couldn't see their expressions clearly in the darkness, but I could see that their bodies were tense.
Fan Laoliu stabbed the long pole into the water without changing his expression, and then pulled it out: "Tree roots. What a fuss." He turned back and glared at his disciples, but He Chengju noticed that his hand holding the long pole tightened.
The boat continued forward.
The fog became thicker and thicker, and the lights on the shore were completely invisible. Only the moon shed a layer of pale white light through the fog layer. The barren graves on both sides of the bank were looming in the fog, and some of the grave heads had collapsed, exposing half of the coffin boards. Occasionally, a night bird flutters up from the grave, its cry sounding like a baby crying.
He Chengju didn't feel much at all. He doesn't believe in ghosts and gods, he only believes in the knife in his hand. But he could feel that the atmosphere on the boat was changing - the breathing of the apprentices was obviously faster, and the paddling movements became stiff.
"Don't panic." He Chengju's voice was not loud, but it carried far across the quiet river. "Dead people don't bite, living people do. Focus on the living."
